key_insight: Predicting welding distortion in large metallic structures requires application-specific trade-offs between accuracy, computational cost and calibration.
engineering_relevance: Design-stage welding sequence optimisation and structural planning offer the strongest opportunities to reduce distortion and costly corrective work.
method: Review research from 2000–2025 on large-structure distortion prediction and control.
Compare thermo-elasto-plastic finite element, inherent strain and local/global modelling approaches.
Assess emerging data-driven surrogates and design-stage, in-process and post-weld mitigation.
evidence_signal: Approximately 10% and 1% of reviewed references address large aluminium and high-strength steel structures, respectively, indicating limited evidence beyond conventional structural steels.
watch_item: No prediction approach is universally transferable; industrial deployment remains constrained by calibration needs, scalability and data availability.
paper_title: A review of prediction and control methods on welding-induced distortions in large metallic structures
